title: Onramp playbook for open-models with pin safety layers and compatibility signals
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: New open-model submissions vary widely in stability, runtime characteristics, and compatibility with Redwood runtime features (quantization, KV cache, streaming). We need a concise, operational playbook — an 'onramp' — that clarifies minimum metadata, automated sanity checks, progressive pinning rules, and rollback criteria so catalog engineers and runtime can onboard models safely without frequent manual gatekeeping.

Goal: Deliver a single-page onboarding playbook + machine-readable checklist that: (1) defines the minimum compatibility signals required for automatic admission, (2) specifies safety layers for pinning (soft pin -> observe -> hard pin), (3) enumerates runtime integration validation steps, (4) details acceptance criteria and rollback triggers, and (5) plugs into existing intake UI and ingestion CI. The playbook must be operational for both hosted and Dedicated/Private flows and produce clear telemetry to the Console.

Scope decisions: This ticket focuses on the product-side acceptance rules and playbook. Engineering work to implement the automated checks (CI jobs, runtime probes) and Console UI wiring will be captured as dependent ENG tickets. Security/QoS checks (KMS, audit) are out-of-scope for this PRD but listed as blockers if required by specific customers.

Non-goals: Full runtime kernel selection logic, quantization autotuning, or model quality grading/evals. Those are separate initiatives but will be referenced as integration points.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page 'Onramp Playbook' doc in Confluence that defines: minimal metadata, mandatory compatibility signals, pinning stages, and rollback triggers.
A machine-readable checklist (YAML) stored in the catalog repo describing the gate rules for automatic admission; checklist accepted by eng during grooming.
Clear mapping of compatibility signals to runtime probes (e.g., max_seq, memory_estimate, operator_support) and expected pass/fail behavior.
Pin safety layer defined: soft-pin (informational), staged-observe (telemetry + 48h), hard-pin (pinned in catalog with rollout constraints).
Rollback criteria and automated sentinel checks (latency regression >20% quantile or error rate spike) with concrete actions (unpin, re-queue for manual review).
Owner and on-call rotation for onboarding incidents documented (who to page when an ingress causes regressions).
Acceptance checklist reviewed and approved in PM/Runtime/Platform sync (meeting notes linked) and routed to engineering for implementation plan.
An initial intake flow change request (Console UI) scoped and linked to a follow-up ENG ticket for wiring the checklist to the UI.
Telemetry wires: defined set of metrics to emit on first 1,000 requests for new model variants (latency p50/p95, error_rate, memory_oob), and dashboard template created in Grafana/Console.
The playbook includes at least 3 worked examples (LLM chat model, small embedding model, experimental quantized variant) demonstrating decisions and pin transitions.
